div.head: Grið 7
div.ab: 7 on þam lagum is arcebiscopes feoh endlyfangylde 7 cynges is nigongylde.
And on þam lagum is arcebiscopes feoh endlyfangylde and cynges is nigongylde.
Und in jenen Gesetzen ist des Erzbischofs Gut eilffach und das des Königs ist neunfach [zu entgelten].
And in those laws the archbishop's property [is to be paid for] elevenfold and the king's ninefold.
And according to those laws, elevenfold compensation is due for the archbishop’s property and ninefold for the king’s.

note.label: echoes
note.quote: This is the only surviving clause in Old English law to echo the first clause of Æthelbert’s legislation

div.note: This is the only surviving clause in Old English law to echo the first clause of Æthelbert’s legislation, the earliest royal law code, though it is significant that Wulfstan assigns compensation to the archbishop, rather than to a bishop, as in the earlier text. Moreover, Æthelbert’s laws do not mention the king, implying that one purpose of this clause may be to promote the church at the expense of the secular aristocracy.
